[Course context]
(Week 1) A language model learns patterns in language. Given some text, it predicts what is likely to come next. LLMs generate text one token at a time: read the prompt, predict the most likely next token, add it, repeat.

[Conversation so far]
(none)

[Student]
What is next-token prediction?

Let's build it from something you already do. Finish this sentence: "The student opened the textbook because she wanted to ___". How did you choose your word, and what would a model need to repeat to turn one predicted word into a whole paragraph?

[Course context]
(Week 7) In supervised fine-tuning the loss is usually focused on the response: prompt tokens are masked (ignored) in the loss and response tokens are scored, so the model learns to produce the answer rather than copy the prompt. This is different from the Week 3 causal mask and the Week 6 padding attention mask.

[Conversation so far]
Student: Why do we mask prompt tokens in instruction fine-tuning?

[Student]
We mask the prompt so the model can't see the instruction.

Careful: this course uses three different masks. The Week 3 causal mask hides future tokens, the Week 6 attention mask hides padding, and the Week 7 mask works in the loss. The model does see the instruction, so which tokens should it be scored on?
